I realized I had lied to the psychiatrist when he asked if my mental battles had any bipolar depression involved. At the time I associated the word bipolar with crazy, so I lied in fear of having that stereotype placed on me.

At this point I was aware that not only did I suffer from depression, but also anxiety and bipolar depression. I was never clinically diagnosed with these but learned about my sufferings with them through my own research.

I was clinically diagnosed with depression and began taking an antidepressant. The medicine began to work, and I started to see improvements. Then I made the mistake of thinking I was able to stop taking my medicine just because I was feeling better.

I would go on to have another depression stint in my senior year of high school. I still hadn’t learned about what had been crippling me. I then went off to college and had off and on bouts with depression.

I lied to doctors about how I was feeling because I had been taught that a man isn’t supposed to show emotions or have feelings. I didn’t want anyone thinking I was soft, so I kept mostly everything to myself.

If you’ve ever suffered from any mental illness or from general stress, this thread is for you. I hope to inspire you. I’ve struggled with anxiety and bipolar depression ever since I was in elementary school. Back then I had no idea about mental illness.
